record.paper_title: Multiparty Quantum Key Agreement: Architectures, State-of-the-art, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can fully device-independent multiparty quantum key agreement be realized in a way that guarantees both secrecy and fairness solely from observed multipartite nonlocal correlations, despite untrusted devices, insider coalitions, and practical constraints such as loophole-free multipartite Bell tests; and what semi-device-independent or measurement-device-independent pathways provide experimentally realistic approximations to that goal?

evidence.quote: Fully device-independent MQKA (DI-MQKA) represents the most ambitious point in the security-model spectrum, aiming for protocols whose secrecy and fairness guarantees rely only on observed nonlocal correlations, such as Bell-inequality violations, and not on any detailed assumptions about the internal workings of sources or detectors.
This intertwining of device assumptions, nonlocality, and game-theoretic fairness makes device-independent MQKA an open and challenging research frontier.

The concept of full device-independent multiparty quantum key agreement (DI-MQKA) represents a theoretically clean goal aimed at guaranteeing security and fairness based solely on observed nonlocal correlations.
One promising pathway is the semi-device-independent MQKA, where the sources are trusted, but the measurement processes are not.
Finally, the emergence of loophole-free Bell tests has provided a robust foundation for device-independent protocols.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider $n \geq 3$ mutually distrustful parties $P_1, \ldots, P_n$ who wish to agree on a common secret bit string $K \in \{0,1\}^\ell$ via a quantum protocol. Each party holds an untrusted measurement device (a black box accepting classical inputs and returning classical outputs) and access to quantum states distributed by an untrusted source over an authenticated classical broadcast channel. Let $P(a_1,\ldots,a_n \mid x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ denote the joint conditional distribution of outputs $a_i$ given inputs $x_i$ realized by the devices in a given run.

A multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol is fully device-independent (DI) if its security and correctness guarantees are derived solely from statistical features of $P$ (e.g., violations of multipartite Bell-type inequalities), without any assumption on the Hilbert-space dimension, the internal state preparation, or the form of measurements implemented by the devices. The protocol must satisfy:

(i) Correctness: with probability at least $1-\varepsilon_c$, all honest parties output the same key $K$.

(ii) Secrecy (against an eavesdropper Eve and against any coalition $C \subsetneq \{P_1,\ldots,P_n\}$ of dishonest insiders, possibly controlling the source and devices of $C$): the trace distance between the joint state of $K$ and the side information held by Eve $\cup\, C$, conditioned on the protocol not aborting, is at most $\varepsilon_s$.

(iii) Fairness: no proper subset of parties (honest or dishonest) can bias the final key toward a value of their choice; formally, for every proper coalition $C$, the conditional distribution of $K$ given $C$'s view is $\varepsilon_f$-close to uniform on $\{0,1\}^\ell$, and every honest party contributes equally to $K$ in a sense made precise by a chosen fairness functional.

Question. Does there exist an $n$-party protocol $(n \geq 3)$ in this fully device-independent model that, given only the observed $n$-partite nonlocal correlations $P$, simultaneously achieves correctness, secrecy, and fairness with $\varepsilon_c, \varepsilon_s, \varepsilon_f \to 0$ in the asymptotic limit, while remaining robust to (a) loophole-free multipartite Bell-test constraints (finite detection efficiency, finite statistics, no signaling), (b) arbitrary insider coalitions $C$ of size up to $n-1$, and (c) bounded quantum and classical resources? In particular, exhibit such a protocol together with a positive secret-key rate as a function of the observed Bell-inequality violation, or prove an impossibility result.

Subproblem. Identify semi-device-independent variants—e.g., where sources are trusted but measurements are untrusted (measurement-device-independent MQKA), or where the Hilbert-space dimension is bounded—under which the above three guarantees can be provably achieved with experimentally realistic parameters, and quantify the trade-off between the strength of the relaxed device assumptions and the achievable key rate.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature treats fully device-independent multiparty quantum key agreement (DI-MQKA) as an active, unresolved research frontier. Device-independent conference key agreement protocols using GHZ states and generalized CHSH-type inequalities have been proposed, and measurement-device-independent and semi-DI MQKA schemes exist, but no protocol simultaneously establishes secrecy, fairness against arbitrary insider coalitions, and loophole-free experimental feasibility. Surveys identify DI-MQKA among the principal open challenges for future quantum-internet key agreement.

status_evidence.title: Advances in device-independent quantum key distribution
status_evidence.snippet: Multipartite DI-QKD/conference key agreement uses generalized CHSH inequalities with GHZ states; full multiparty device independence remains a developing area.
status_evidence.claim: DI conference/multiparty key agreement is an active research direction with open theoretical and experimental challenges.

status_evidence.title: Fundamental limitations on the device-independent quantum conference key agreement
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes upper bounds on achievable rates for DI conference key agreement, indicating fundamental limitations rather than a complete construction.
status_evidence.claim: Known results give rate limitations but not a fully satisfactory DI-MQKA protocol with fairness.

status_evidence.title: Measurement-device-independent multi-party quantum key agreement
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes MDI-MQKA schemes as a semi-device-independent pathway, leaving full DI-MQKA open.
status_evidence.claim: MDI-MQKA serves as a partial / semi-DI pathway toward the full DI-MQKA goal.
